title: Example 13-1: Poetic Lines within Narrative Text

illustrates.quote: Follow print when poetry is embedded within narrative text. a. Retain font attributes. b. Follow print use for either a slash or vertical line to indicate where one poetic line ends and another begins. c. Follow print for spacing of symbols, which may begin or end a braille line. Identify the use of the symbols on the Special Symbols page, or in a transcriber’s note before the text.

blocks.text: … suggesting that “the trust Othello puts him in / On some odd time of his infirmity / Will shake this island”
blocks.features: Leading ellipsis shows this is a mid-sentence excerpt from a longer narrative discussion (about Shakespeare's Othello); the quoted poetic fragment uses a slash to mark where each of the three poetic lines ends, run in with the surrounding narrative prose.

print.notes: The print original is a picture (PDF p.356, boxed example) with no selectable text layer; transcribed here by reading the image.
